مُدَمْلَجٌ i. q. مُدْرَجٌ أَمْلَسُ [Round, as though rolled like a scroll, and smooth]: (S, K:) and a stone, and a solid hoof, smooth and round; as also مُدَمْلَقُ and مُدَمْلَكٌ. (S in art. دملق.) A rájiz says, (S, TA,) namely, El-'Ajjáj, (so in a copy of the S,) “كَأَنَّ مِنْهَا القَصَبَ المُدَمْلَجَا
سُوقٌ مِنَ البَرْدِىِّ مَا تَعَوَّجَا
” [app. describing a certain animal, or animals, and meaning As though her, or their, round and smooth leg-bones were stalks of the papyrus, not crooked]. (S, TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
